scope: Fail-closed byte-bound validation of the released ActionBench tensor, camera and RGBA frame structures after successful snapshot admission. This is engineering input qualification only; it is not inference, scoring, tracked-correspondence proof, runtime compatibility or scientific evidence.

required_snapshot_admission.rule: Every camera.json, surfaces.npy and PNG consumed by this semantic pass must re-match its size and SHA-256 in the successful snapshot admission.

surfaces.normal_policy: Require finite floating values and report norm extrema/zero count; the public README names these columns as normals but does not publish a unit-normal tolerance, so no invented norm threshold is applied.
surfaces.tracked_correspondence_policy: The public README states that point indices are tracked through time. File structure cannot independently prove semantic correspondence, so this remains a source claim and is not promoted by this admission.

camera.projection_convention: X_cam = X @ R^T + T; camera looks along -Z

frames.encoding: PNG colour type 6 (RGBA), 8 or 16 bits per channel, valid standard compression/filter/interlace mode
frames.geometry: positive square dimensions and identical IHDR encoding within each 16-frame sample; population-wide encoding variants are recorded rather than forbidden
frames.alpha_semantics_limit: RGBA encoding proves an alpha channel is present. This admission does not invent a foreground-mask occupancy threshold.

parser_resource_limits.scope: Fail-closed parser memory guards, not scientific data thresholds. The admitted released files are expected to lie below these per-file bounds; exceeding a bound is returned for review rather than loaded into the bounded process.

limitations: The pass rereads roughly 5.3 GB of admitted dataset content and therefore requires a fresh Local wall-time observation; no Web timing is claimed.
It does not deserialize any model, run ActionMesh, export GLBs or invoke the official scorer.
It does not prove that the current public release matches the unpublished leaderboard generation environment.
It cannot authorize or price the 28,800-second queue; a complete current multi-arm generation/export/scoring unit and peak-VRAM receipt remain required.
